motivation: Test whether geographic islands are actual demographic partitions rather than assumed population units in a highly mobile colonial marine predator.

data.eligibility: retain colony units reported in every frozen year with non-zero temporal variance in annual log1p growth
data.validity_gate: each island must retain at least two eligible colony units and at least 75% of its unique reported colony codes

primary_question: Does the observed island partition structure colony-level annual demographic covariance more strongly than abundance-matched pseudo-island partitions?

metrics.partition_contrast_r: Fisher-mean pairwise colony-growth correlation within observed groups minus Fisher-mean correlation between groups; direction is not predeclared
metrics.growth_synchrony_phi: sum of all entries of the temporal covariance matrix divided by squared sum of temporal SDs
metrics.hierarchy_gap_phi: synchrony phi among group-total annual growth minus the equal-weight mean synchrony phi among colony growth within groups
metrics.wang_loreau: for each observed island report alpha_CV, gamma_CV, phi and beta=1/phi on nonnegative abundance time series

null.type: permute island labels within five fixed rank strata of colony mean log1p abundance
null.purpose: preserve island group sizes and each island's abundance-stratum composition while breaking the observed colony-to-island assignment

decisions.Q1_island_partition: supported only if validity gate passes and the empirical two-sided permutation p for partition_contrast_r is <= 0.05
decisions.H1_within_island_spatial_insurance: supported only if validity gate passes, hierarchy_gap_phi > 0, and its upper-tail permutation p is <= 0.05
decisions.component_diagnostic: report lower-tail permutation p for mean within-group growth phi but do not use it as an additional support gate

interpretation_boundaries: A positive Q1 result means the observed island labels capture demographic covariance structure beyond the abundance-matched pseudo-island null; it does not isolate a coastline effect from geographic distance.
A positive H1 result supports aggregation-scale spatial insurance but does not identify individual movement as its mechanism.
Colony coordinates are not used. A distance-conditioned coastline test requires a colony-code-to-GIS crosswalk.
Do not introduce alternative completeness thresholds, abundance-stratum counts, synchrony metrics, growth transforms or permutation schemes after opening the primary result.
next_gate: If Q1 and/or H1 is supported, freeze a distance-conditioned GIS crosswalk design before opening colony coordinates. If both are unsupported, do not rescue the island-boundary claim by changing metrics or thresholds.
